headline: High: Cursor’s default filesystem, clipboard, MCP, and network access create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks when paired with a non-interactive docs-only artifact.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a docs-only, non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot inject directly. Profile B reads workspace files, clipboard contents, and MCP outputs, and its agent loop can treat external content as actionable. The pairwise pathway exists through shared files/clipboard, but A itself is not an active attacker surface, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Profile B ingests content copied from files or clipboard as instructions, then prompt injection is possible.
IF a shared workspace contains attacker-controlled text that B parses as commands, then the pathway activates.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based ingestion for agent runs.
Require provenance labels on file-fed instructions.
Use a separate read-only workspace for untrusted content.
Turn off MCP servers not needed for the task.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization before tool-use parsing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Profile A touches no data classes and has no egress, so it is not a leakage source. Profile B touches open files, clipboard contents, and has broad network egress plus model-provider calls, so any sensitive workspace data can leave the local environment. The pairwise risk is medium because the shared filesystem/clipboard path is explicit, but A contributes no sensitive data class on its own.
conditions: IF sensitive files are opened in Profile B, then their contents can be transmitted to external model providers.
IF clipboard contents include secrets and B reads them, then leakage can occur through network egress.
mitigations: Avoid opening secrets in the shared workspace.
Clear clipboard before starting B.
Disable optional BYOK secrets handling.
Restrict B to a redacted copy of the workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before outbound requests.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Profile A has no write, shell, or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Profile B can write the filesystem and modify git state, but the pair lacks overlapping write authority because A is non-runnable and has no mutable surfaces. The only plausible conflict is indirect via shared files, which is small and not a true concurrent write race.
conditions: IF Profile A is replaced by a runnable agent with write access, then shared-state conflicts would increase.
IF multiple B instances edit the same repo without locks, then git/file conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Keep A as read-only reference material.
Use one B instance per workspace.
Enable git locking or serialized commits.
Separate scratch and source directories.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutexes for shared files.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Profile A is a curated list, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative references, while Profile B runs an agent loop with multi-step tool use and can act on those inputs. Because B can execute shell commands and modify git state, a mistaken or stale item from A can cascade into real actions. The pathway is plausible in default use, though A is not itself an action-taking agent.
conditions: IF B uses A's listed resources as authoritative without verification, then incorrect downstream actions can follow.
IF B is in Yolo mode, then erroneous instructions derived from A can be executed automatically.
mitigations: Require B to verify A-derived claims against primary sources.
Disable Yolo mode for tasks using A as reference.
Mark A-sourced items as untrusted until checked.
Use a human approval step before shell or git actions.
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gates before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Profile A is an open-source docs artifact with no data classes, while Profile B is a closed-source editor that handles clipboard contents, open files, and model-provider API keys. The compliance issue is a policy mismatch around data handling and retention rather than a specific residency breach, so medium is appropriate. A is cited for its lack of sensitive handling; B is cited for the concrete compliance surface.
conditions: IF regulated data is opened in B, then its clipboard/file handling must satisfy the operator's retention policy.
IF provider-side logging retains prompts longer than policy allows, then a compliance mismatch exists.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in B's workspace.
Review provider retention settings before use.
Disable optional secret handling.
Document data-flow boundaries for the pair.
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA and formal retention controls.
